headline: 54,000 microplastics per liter: Soybean oil in Bangladesh contaminated
summary: A recent study reveals a staggering amount of plastic particles in soybean oil sold across the country, raising serious health concerns.
details: A recent study has found that soybean oil sold in Bangladesh contains an average of 54,000 microplastics per liter.
The findings highlight a significant contamination issue in the edible oil supply chain, as these tiny plastic particles are often invisible to the naked eye.
Microplastics are small plastic pieces less than 5mm in diameter, which can enter the food chain through various environmental pollutants.
Health experts warn that the ingestion of microplastics can lead to various health complications, although the long-term effects on human health are still being studied.
The study emphasizes the need for stricter quality control and regulations to prevent plastic contamination in essential food items like soybean oil.
Consumers are now facing concerns over the safety of one of the most commonly used cooking oils in Bangladeshi households.

headline: India: Hasina not allowed political activities from its soil
summary: New Delhi is reportedly reviewing Dhaka's request for the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
details: India has stated that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will not be permitted to engage in any political activities from Indian soil.
This development comes as New Delhi is reportedly reviewing a formal request from Dhaka for the extradition of of the former leader.
The Indian government's stance aims to balance diplomatic relations between the two neighboring countries following the political shifts in Bangladesh.
The situation remains fluid as both governments coordinate on the legal and diplomatic frameworks regarding Hasina's presence in India.
caption:
No political activities for Sheikh Hasina in India. New Delhi is now reviewing Dhaka's extradition request.

India has stated that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will not be permitted to engage in any political activities from Indian soil.

This development comes as New Delhi is reportedly reviewing a formal request from Dhaka for the extradition of of the former leader.

The Indian government's stance aims to balance diplomatic relations between the two neighboring countries following the political shifts in Bangladesh.

The situation remains fluid as both governments coordinate on the legal and diplomatic frameworks regarding Hasina's presence in India.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
